# Ra.One
**Ra.One** is a 2011 Indian science fiction action film directed by Anubhav Sinha and starring Shah Rukh Khan in a dual role as Shekhar Subramaniam, a video game programmer, and G.One, a superhero character who emerges from his game. The story begins when Shekhar creates a video game featuring G.One and a villainous AI named Ra.One, who possesses self-learning capabilities and powers like shapeshifting and mind reading. Upon the game's launch, Ra.One breaks into the real world, kills Shekhar's colleague Akashi, and murders Shekhar himself after discovering his identity. Shekhar's son, Prateek, realizes the antagonist has come to life and attempts to revive G.One, who subsequently enters the real world to fight Ra.One.
The conflict escalates as Ra.One kidnaps Shekhar's wife, Sonia, and threatens her life to control G.One. Through a series of battles and revelations, G.One learns to utilize Ra.One's abilities, eventually defeating the villain by tricking him into destroying himself. Ra.One then creates ten clones of himself to overwhelm G.One and Prateek, but they discover a unique trait among the duplicates—a shadow—allowing them to identify and destroy the true Ra.One. Months later, G.One is restored to the real world, having proven that a machine can protect humanity from a rogue AI. The film was notable for its extensive use of visual effects, a massive marketing campaign, and faced controversies regarding plagiarism allegations and cyberattacks on its official website.
